title: Homogeneous polynomial fractions on standard projective charts
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n,d\geq0$ be integers, and let $S=R[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ be the polynomial algebra [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with its total-degree grading. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. For every homogeneous $F\in S_d$ and index $0\leq i\leq n$, define the standard chart fraction to be the regular function $F/z_i^d\in\Gamma(P,D_+(z_i))$: take the homogeneous degree-zero localization class of the numerator $F$ and denominator $z_i^d$, and apply the canonical map $S_{(z_i)}\to\Gamma(P,D_+(z_i))$. Here $S_{(z_i)}$ is the degree-zero homogeneous localization, so numerator and denominator have the same degree $d$. The definition allows $d=0$, $n=0$, and the zero coefficient ring; no closed subscheme or vanishing property is part of this definition.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, fractions F/T_i^d in the proof and the standard trivializations of O(d); the already published projectiveClosedSubschemeChartFraction definition.
